# Getting Started

> Start testing your MCP server in minutes

> [!NOTE
]\n>\n> SDK 10, CLI 6, Vitest 0.3, and later versions require an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs

with uploads disabled. Earlier versions keep their existing behavior.

## 1. Choose how to open Inspector

Every option below

opens the MCPJam Inspector. Pick one based on where your MCP server runs.

> [card] [Web](https://app.mcpjam.com)
>
> No inst

all. HTTPS servers only. Share servers with your team.

> [card] [Terminal](https://docs.mcpjam.com/installation.md#terminal)
>

> `npx @mcpjam/inspector@latest`. Requires Node.js. HTTP/S and local STDIO.

> [card] [macOS](https://docs.mcpjam.com/installa

tion.md#desktop-app)
>
> Desktop app (`.dmg`). No Node.js. HTTP/S and local STDIO.

> [card] [Windows](https://docs.mcpjam.com

/installation.md#desktop-app)
>
> Desktop app (`.exe` installer). No Node.js. HTTP/S and local STDIO.

> [card] [Docker](https

://docs.mcpjam.com/installation.md#docker)
>
> Pull from Docker Hub. HTTP/S, plus STDIO servers that run inside the container.
\n* **Your server has a public HTTPS URL**: any option works. The web app needs no install.\n* **Your server runs on `localhost` o
r over STDIO**: use Terminal or the macOS or Windows desktop app. The web app can't reach it.\n* **You want Inspector isolated in
a container**: use Docker. Reach servers on your machine at `http://host.docker.internal:PORT`, and note that STDIO commands run i
nside the container, not on your machine.\n\nSee [Installation](https://docs.mcpjam.com/installation.md#which-one-do-i-need) for t

he full comparison.

## 2. Connect a server

On first launch, MCPJam shows a **Welcome** overlay that guides you through conne
cting your first server. You can:\n\n* **Enter your own server**: paste an HTTPS URL (e.g. `https://your-server.example/mcp`) or a
STDIO command (Terminal, Desktop, and Docker only).\n* **Try the Excalidraw demo**: a hosted diagramming MCP app, no setup requir
ed.\n\nAfter connecting, MCPJam shows the server name and tool count, then offers an **Open Playground** button that seeds the cha

t with the prompt:

```
What can this server do?
```

Press **Send** to explore your server's tools. No API key, ngrok, or C

hatGPT/Claude subscription needed.

> [!TIP]
>
> You should see your server show **Connected** and its tools listed in the Pla

yground's left rail.

> [!TIP]
>
> Use the widget debug icons to open tool input/output, CSP activity, widget state, and JSON-

RPC for each result.

## 3. Connect your own server

Open the **Connect** tab in the left sidebar (labelled **Servers** in som
e builds). Click **Add server**.\n\n* **HTTP**: Paste a URL ending in `/mcp`. The web app accepts **HTTPS** URLs only. Terminal, D
esktop, and Docker accept **HTTP** or **HTTPS**; from Docker, use `host.docker.internal` for servers on your machine. Add a bearer
token or use the [OAuth Debugger](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/guided-oauth.md) if the server requires auth.\n* **STDIO** (T
erminal, Desktop, and Docker): Paste a command such as `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything`. In Docker the command run
s inside the container. Not available in the web app. See [Hosted App](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md).\n\nEach **Conn
ected** server is available in the Playground, Tools, Prompts, and Resources. Connect more from the **Connect** tab anytime.\n\n>
[!TIP]\n>\n> You should see your server show **Connected** with a green dot in the **Connect** tab, and its tools should appear in
the Playground's left rail.\n\n## 4. Where to go next", "is_error": false}]}, "parent_tool_use_id": null, "session_id": "059965c1
